analysis: Examined fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json base text (lines 1-2004) and the supplied patch excerpt. Visible changes are test-fixture updates: the prompt_contract_id changes from 6bb9fb05... to 8171fec3... at the model level (line 7) and in each case's plan (e.g. lines 72, 239, 363, 454, 566, 831, 1270, 1370, 1680), plus block-boundary chain_hash changes at lines 836/839. The changed-range list shows many further single-line edits (prompt_token_count, chain hashes, and so on) beyond the supplied text. Only base text and a truncated patch were provided, so the head-side values and the corresponding Swift or Go prompt-contract code were not visible. The fixture is a golden-vector data file, not runtime code, so it introduces no new attack surface of its own. The changed contract ID is relevant to the cache-sharing threat T-041, because cache_routing_eligible and the chain hashes feed prefix-cache keying. The rotation is the intended invalidation mechanism for a changed prompt template or normalization, so it makes cross-contract cache reuse less likely rather than more. The fixture content (assistant Harmony framing stripping, tool argument null handling, boolean-schema conversion) is an existing contract that the PR may modify. Without head text I cannot confirm that the new vectors preserve the stripping or sanitization behavior, for example that assistant-supplied channel/harmony control tokens remain neutralized in template_input. The next pass should check the source change that generates the new contract ID, and that it is bumped whenever the template or normalization changes. It should also confirm the vectors were regenerated rather than hand-edited to match a regressed implementation. No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
